MISO requests that the Commission accept the proposed revisions effective 90 days from 
the date of this filing (i.e., February 14, 2027).  MISO recognizes this filing includes significant 
Tariff revisions and introduces new processes and cost recovery mechanisms that impact the 
broader stakeholder community.  In response to OMS and other stakeholder requests for MISO to 
support an extended comment period, MISO proposes a 30-day comment period to allow 
stakeholders sufficient time to evaluate and comment on the proposals being presented in this 
filing.  This extended comment period reasonably balances the need for additional time for 
stakeholder review while maintaining the urgency presented by the Show Cause Order and works 
well within MISO’s requested 90-day effective date request.  
 
I. 
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY 
 
MISO to date has been able to successfully manage the integration of large loads leveraging 
existing MISO tools and quickly recognized the need for additional frameworks and processes to 
support reliable, efficient, and cost-effective integration given projected trends for f faster and 
dramatic demand growth across the region.  To this end, MISO, its Transmission Owners, state 
regulatory authorities, and broad stakeholder community have been working collaboratively to 
support the reliable, cost-effective, and efficient integration of large loads.  Over the past two years 
MISO has been developing new processes and tools to provide additional transparency, efficient 
reliability standardization, integrated solutions for generation and new transmission service 
offerings with stakeholders to meet the challenge.  The MISO Large Load Working Group has 
been an effective clearing house for such efforts and is providing a constructive, collaborative 
forum to develop these solutions.  This group met over thirteen times in the last eight months with 
an average of 400 people and a peak of 1000 people participating in each session.  This process 
included over 100 MISO presentations to stakeholders and over 400 feedback responses from 
stakeholders. 
   
MISO recognizes the need for balanced solutions to support the diverse interests of 
stakeholders and state policies across the MISO region.  While these differing perspectives can 
make unanimity- difficult to achieve, they contribute to a robust stakeholder process and better-
informed outcomes that ultimately drive the enormous value that MISO membership brings to 
customers in terms of reliability, cost-effectiveness and policy enablement. 
  
The Commission’s Show Cause Order provided important support for MISO’s ongoing 
efforts to develop solutions for responsible and reliable integration of large loads.  By identifying 
specific priorities and encouraging incremental filings as solutions matured, the Commission 
established a framework that enabled stakeholders and MISO to advance improvements without 
waiting for a single comprehensive package.

In response, MISO has already filed several proposals responsive to the Show Cause Order 
that are currently pending before the Commission, including Zero Injection-GIA, Large Load 
Interconnection Reliability Requirements, and the Load Additions Resource Study.  Collectively 
these filings represent meaningful progress toward more timely, transparent, reliable, and cost-
effective large load integration, which appropriately mitigates cost shifts to other Transmission 
Customers.   
  
The additional package of solutions in this filing and the companion filing11 complement 
MISO’s pending Large Load filings and directly address the remaining concerns identified in the 
Show Cause Order.  MISO’s filings, in the aggregate, reflect its compliance with the timelines and 
scope of the Show Cause Order.  At the same time, MISO recognizes that Large Load integration 
will continue to evolve.  These filings represent an important milestone, not an endpoint.  MISO 
remains committed to further enhancing its planning, operational, and market frameworks as 
experience is gained and system needs grow.  The Large Load Working Group will continue to 
serve as the primary stakeholder forum for evaluating, developing and refining additional solutions 
to support ongoing integration of Large Loads across the MISO region. 
  
The filings before the Commission are the product of an extremely robust, albeit expedited, 
stakeholder process conducted within the timelines established by the Show Cause Order.  MISO 
advanced solutions that incorporated substantial stakeholder feedback while remaining consistent 
with MISO’s filing rights and jurisdictional responsibilities.  MISO worked closely with its 
Transmission Owners to develop this joint filing and appropriately recognize their respective roles, 
rights, and responsibilities.  MISO also engaged the Organization of MISO states through regular 
discussions throughout the development of this package of filings.  
 
While full alignment was not achieved on every aspect of the proposals, stakeholder and 
state regulator input materially informed the resulting framework.  MISO is confident that the 
collective set of filings before the Commission provides state regulators with additional 
transparency, information and tools to help fulfill their responsibilities to retail electricity 
customers, consistent with the objectives outlined in the Show Cause Order.  The solutions also 
preserve flexibility for states to advance their individual policy objectives, including the use of 
detailed information and analyses provided through MISO’s planning and operational processes. 
 
The proposals included in the filing provide a robust foundation for integrating Large 
Loads in a manner that supports reliability, protects Transmission Customers from cost shifts 
related to new Large Loads, and provides additional transmission service options consistent with 
the Commission’s objectives for co-located loads, behind the meter generation arrangements and 
flexible Large Loads.  Specifically, this filing addresses the following elements identified in the 
Show Cause Order:

• Large Load Project Review (LLPR) – The LLPR establishes a comprehensive application 
and evaluation process to assess the grid impacts associated with Transmission Service 
needed to serve proposed Large Loads, including required Network Upgrades and 
associated costs.  The LLPR also includes deposits, project milestones, and other 
safeguards designed to discourage speculative Large Load requests.  
• Large Load Transparency Dashboard – The results of the LLPR periodically will be 
published to provide transparency into the location and estimated costs associated with 
Large Load facilities in the MISO region, while protecting confidential information. 
• Cost Shifting Risk Among Transmission Customers – MISO and the MISO Transmission 
Owners have developed new Tariff language and pro forma cost recovery agreements 
designed to ensure that the costs incurred to provide Transmission Service to Large Load 
Transmission Customers, including the costs of Large Load Upgrades (defined herein), are 
born by such customers and thereby avoid unfair cost shifts among Transmission 
Customers.  The agreements leave retail regulatory authorities able to further disaggregate 
costs as warranted. 
• Additional Transmission Services – The new Transmission Services available to Large 
Loads include Firm Service Step Up and Interim Non-Firm NITS service.  These offerings  
build off existing NITS service and support the timely integration of Large Loads by 
aligning Transmission Service with a Transmission Customer’s projected buildout and 
operational needs, while providing flexibility in how Transmission Service is obtained 
during different stages of development. 
 
MISO appreciates the guidance provided by the Commission in the Show Cause Order and 
believes this filing, together with the companion GRITS filing, and MISO’s other pending Large 
Load filings fully addresses the concerns identified by the Commission.  Taken together, these 
proposals represent a significant advancement in framework supporting Large Load integration, 
building on processes and tools that MISO has already implemented.   
 
At the same time, MISO recognizes that the rapid growth of Large Loads will continue to 
present new challenges and opportunities.  As a result, these filings should be viewed as an 
important milestone rather than an endpoint. MISO remains committed to working collaboratively 
with stakeholders, Transmission Owners, states and the Commission to evaluate and develop 
additional tools, processes, and solutions to support the reliable, efficient, transparent and cost-
effective integration and operation of Large Loads in the MISO region.  
 
II. 
BACKGROUND  
 
This omnibus filing brings together the history and substance of MISO’s response to the 
Commission’s Show Cause Order.  MISO has pursued that response through a series of related 
filings, submitting individual proposals as the necessary information, stakeholder consideration, 
and proposed Tariff provisions became sufficiently developed.  The earlier submissions addressed 
components that were ready to proceed while work continued on other elements of the response.  
This filing explains that progression, describes the relationship among the proposals already

submitted, and presents the additional provisions that have since been developed.  The background 
below traces how that coordinated effort led to the present submission. 
 
A. The changing nature of load growth in the MISO region. 
 
The MISO region is experiencing a change in the scale, concentration, and pace of new 
electricity demand.  Large Load additions, including data centers and advanced manufacturing 
facilities, can introduce substantial demand at a single location and seek service on schedules that 
are shorter than those traditionally required to develop supporting generation and transmission 
infrastructure.  These developments require MISO, the Transmission Owners, and the entities 
serving those Loads to coordinate planning, investment, and operational requirements early in the 
development process to address the unique needs associated with such Large Load additions to the 
grid.  As MISO explained in its July 20, 2026, Informational Report, conventional forecasting 
methods were developed for more gradual and geographically dispersed growth; Large Load 
projects present additional uncertainty concerning location, timing, and the demand that ultimately 
materializes.12 
 
The resulting challenge extends beyond identifying a physical point of connection.  MISO 
must assess the transmission facilities needed to serve new demand, understand how the Load will 
behave during normal operations and system disturbances, and coordinate the addition of resources 
needed to support resource adequacy.  At the same time, the uncertainty surrounding Large Load 
development makes it necessary to distinguish committed projects from speculative requests and 
to address the risk that investments made to serve a particular load may remain unrecovered if that 
Load is delayed, reduced, or does not materialize.  MISO’s Large Load initiatives were developed 
to address these related planning, reliability, and cost recovery concerns.13 
 
MISO has also recognized that certain Large Loads may be willing and able to limit their 
withdrawals from the Transmission System.  That flexibility can support service before all 
facilities needed for full firm service have been completed, or an ongoing arrangement under which 
only a portion of the Load receives firm service.  Accommodating those different needs requires 
clear service rights, enforceable operating limits, and appropriate treatment of the customer’s 
planning and financial obligations.  The development of additional Transmission Service options 
therefore became a component of MISO’s broader Large Load work. 
 
B. MISO’s existing processes and the development of a dedicated stakeholder forum. 
 
MISO’s efforts to address these challenges began before the Commission issued its Show 
Cause Order.  MISO had improved the Expedited Project Review (“EPR”) process within the

MISO also began consolidating stakeholder consideration of large load issues.  Following 
a January 2026 Large Load Additions Workshop, MISO’s Steering Committee approved creation 
of the Large Load Working Group (“LLWG”) in March 2026.  The LLWG held its first meeting

into a coordinated large load work plan.17 
 
C. The Show Cause Order and the opportunity to develop regional solutions. 
 
On June 18, 2026, the Commission instituted a proceeding under section 206 of the Federal 
Power Act (“FPA”) to examine whether MISO’s Tariff remained just and reasonable in light of 
various concerns related to large and co-located load development.  The Commission identified 
concerns regarding application and study procedures, operational requirements, network upgrade 
cost transparency and recovery, service for flexible and co-located loads, and generation serving 
associated Loads.  It directed MISO and the Transmission Owners to respond to its preliminary 
findings and address potential Tariff changes.18 
 
The Commission’s action reinforced work already underway while identifying additional 
matters for stakeholder consideration.  The Show Cause Order also contemplated development of 
regional solutions through FPA section 205 filings and allowed requests for an abeyance of up to

On July 20, 2026, MISO submitted the Informational Report addressing resource adequacy

On August 3, 2026, MISO requested that the proceeding be held in abeyance for 90 days.  
The Abeyance Motion described a series of anticipated section 205 filings covering Zero-Injection 
Interconnection Service, a Large Load definition and Interconnection Reliability Requirements,

The Commission granted the requested abeyance on August 14, 2026.  It found that the

and held the proceeding, including the responses and briefing questions, in abeyance for 90 days.22  
The Commission established November 16, 2026 as the revised response deadline and explained 
that a timely FPA section 205 filing addressing its preliminary findings would suspend the filing 
respondents’ obligation to respond and continue the abeyance pending further Commission 
direction.  The Commission further explained that any issues not addressed by the FPA section 
205 filings would remain subject to the FPA section 206 proceeding instituted under the Show 
Cause Order and encouraged respondents seeking termination to identify specifically which 
proposed revisions resolved which concerns.23 
 
D. The earlier filings and the matters reserved for further development. 
 
During the abeyance period, MISO submitted proposals addressing those elements of its 
response that were sufficiently developed for Commission review.  Those submissions did not 
purport to resolve every issue in a single filing.  Instead, they advanced particular components 
while expressly identifying related matters for further development and subsequent submission.

First, on August 18, 2026, MISO submitted its Zero Injection Generator Interconnection 
Agreement (“ZGIA”) proposal in Docket No. ER26-3552-000.  The filing proposed a form of 
Generator Interconnection Agreement, a study process, and an agreement for generation serving 
Load at the same substation without broader injections onto the Transmission System.  MISO had 
begun developing the concept before the Show Cause Order and refined it through stakeholder 
discussion.  MISO limited the initial proposal to same-substation arrangements so that the zero 
injection option could proceed while the separate questions presented by generation serving 
electrically proximate Load were addressed through further work.25  The ZGIA proposal was 
deliberately limited in scope.  This distinction is relevant to the present filing because a generator 
interconnection pathway alone does not supply the complete Transmission Service and cost 
recovery framework for the Load it serves.26 
 
Second, on August 28, 2026, MISO submitted its Interconnection Reliability Requirements 
(“IRR”) for Large Loads proposal in Docket No. ER26-3650-000.  That proposal included a Tariff

operational visibility, together with phasor measurement, ramp, and ride-through requirements for

Customer taking service on behalf of the Large Load, reflecting that customer’s direct relationship 
with MISO.  The proposal was intended to improve MISO’s ability to assess, observe, and manage 
Large Load behavior.27  The IRR filing also distinguished requirements applicable to the 
Transmission Customer taking Transmission Service on behalf of the Large Load from the study 
procedures used to identify system-level impacts and necessary transmission solutions.  MISO 
explained that it already performed stability assessments through MTEP and EPR but would 
address enhancements to the broader Load addition and Transmission Service study processes in 
a later FPA section 205 filing.  The IRR proposal thus supplied the proposed operational 
requirements to be incorporated into, and assessed through, the developing study framework.28

proposal built upon experience with expedited load-side planning and coordinated the Load and 
generation studies through a common application framework.  It complemented ZGIA by

E. The additional provisions now presented in this omnibus filing. 
 
While the ZGIA, IRR, and LARS proposals proceeded through separate filings, MISO 
continued developing the remaining application, study, service, and financial provisions.  Those 
matters required additional information and coordination concerning how customers would request 
service, how the necessary upgrades would be identified, what obligations would support the 
resulting investment, and what service could be provided under differing operating conditions.  
The present filing brings forward those additional proposals and explains how they relate to the 
components previously submitted. The proposed LLPR process builds on the load-specific 
functions of EPR to establish a dedicated Tariff framework for a Transmission Customer taking 
service on behalf of a Large Load to obtain Transmission Service. The LLPR includes standardized 
applications, recurring study cycles, identification of necessary Upgrades, and the integration of 
the proposed interconnection reliability requirements.31  While only Transmission Owners were 
eligible to submit requests to the EPR process, MISO is proposing that only Large Load 
Transmission Customers (in collaboration with the Transmission Owner) may submit an 
application to the LLPR process.  
 
The cost recovery and transparency provisions ensure the Large Load Transmission 
Customer pays the cost of the Large Load Upgrades required to provide Transmission Service, 
including if the expected Load does not arrive as anticipated or remain in service.  The proposed 
cost recovery agreements, related security, and cost transparency measures are intended to connect 
the requested Transmission Service and necessary supporting investment with enforceable 
financial obligations.  The proposed framework includes Tariff revisions and a pro forma Large 
Load Cost Recovery Agreement, and a pro forma Large Load Impacted Transmission Owner Cost 
Recovery Agreement, together with a publicly accessible dashboard providing high-level 
information about upgrades and estimated costs while protecting confidential information.32

The service proposals address the separate question of how a customer may use the

Accordingly, this omnibus filing should be considered in the context of the full sequence 
of MISO’s submissions in response to the Show Cause Order.  The earlier filings addressed 
components that could be brought forward first; the proposals submitted here reflect the further 
development of the application, study, cost recovery, transparency, and service provisions 
described above.  Together, that history explains both the timing and the scope of the present filing.  
The sections that follow identify the relief sought, describe the additional Tariff revisions proposed 
here, and explain how this submission and the previously filed proposals comprehensively address 
the Commission’s concerns identified in the Show Cause Order. 
 
III. 
LARGE LOAD APPLICATION AND STUDY PROCESS

TRANSMISSION SERVICE OFFERINGS 
 
A. Overview and service selection. 
 
MISO proposes transmission service options that distinguish a customer seeking temporary 
non-firm transmission service while progressing toward full NITS from a customer electing an 
ongoing permanent firm and non-firm service mix.  Firm Service Step Up (“FSSU”) permits NITS 
service to increase as the required capability becomes available.  Interim NITS permits 
transmission service within approved non-firm limits while the remaining upgrades needed for full 
NITS are completed.   
 
The transmission service election determines the customer’s rights and obligations.  
Firmness addresses the availability and priority of Transmission Service; Resource Adequacy 
addresses the capacity needed to support demand.  The proposal treats those questions separately.  
Interim NITS remains in the capacity construct because it is a transition to full NITS service.  
Neither election authorizes withdrawals beyond the quantities and operating conditions established 
for that service. 
 
B. Firm Service Step Up. 
 
The FSSU process is designed to allow a Transmission Customer to obtain NITS in 
increments before all upgrades supporting its ultimate NITS requirement have been completed.  
As the relevant capability becomes available, a portion of the customer’s Interim NITS, described 
further below,  may convert to NITS while the remaining portion continues under the applicable 
interim restrictions.  The customer therefore can use available firm capability without assuming a 
firm entitlement to the full quantity before the system can support that service. 
 
The FSSU process is optional and allows NITS to be combined with Interim NITS.  At 
each step, the applicable firm NITS quantity remains tied to the capability supporting that step; 
any remaining interim quantity continues to be subject to its non-firm, Interim NITS, limits.  This 
distinction preserves the integrity of the service actually available while accommodating a 
customer’s phased development toward full NITS.171 
 
FSSU provides speed to power because it enables faster integration of incremental amounts 
of Large Load using firm service or Interim NITS.  Ms. Xie explains that an FSSU request may 
include a firm service component and Interim NITS component, allowing a portion of the 
customer’s non-firm service to convert to firm service before all required Upgrades are complete, 
with the remaining non-firm service continuing under the applicable Interim NITS operating 
limits.172  The FSSU proposal thus provides an expeditious option to obtain firm service, at least 
in part.
